The book

Bulletproof Knowledge.

Building Hallucination-Resistant Neurosymbolic Agents with Lean and Logic Programming.

By Volodymyr Pavlyshyn

What may your agent remember?
What may it claim?

An agent’s memory can preserve a mistake long after the conversation that created it. This book explores an engineering response: make accepted state changes and answers carry evidence for explicit rules.

Begin with Lean types and a small ontology. Introduce dependent types, invariants, higher-order logic, and λProlog. Build toward an agent whose symbolic checks can reject a proposed fact or answer and explain which obligation failed.

Three ideas to take into your work.

  1. Model knowledge precisely. Give entities, relations, and admissible states an explicit type-level contract.
  2. Separate search from checking. Allow a flexible component to propose evidence while a smaller trusted component checks it.
  3. State the limit honestly. A derivation is relative to the chosen definitions and axioms. It does not turn an unverified observation into a true one.
Companion code, examples, and build instructions are available in the public repository. Follow its pinned toolchain when running the book’s examples.
